label: Terminal · Yard Security Grader
title: Grade your yard

layers.name: Digital Check-in
layers.caption: Layer 00 replaces paper with an auditable, attributed record of every gate event.
layers.rec_why: Without a digital baseline there is no reliable record, and every layer above it is building on sand.

questions.question: Every gate entry is captured digitally, timestamped, and attributed (not on paper).
Trailer and asset IDs and condition are captured by computer vision, without manual entry.
You can search gate history by carrier, driver, asset, or time.

layers.rec_start: capturing every entry digitally, timestamped and attributed
layers.exposure_copy: Without a digital baseline, there is no reliable record of who or what entered. Paper logs go missing or get edited, and every layer above this one is building on sand.
layers.standard_copy: Every entry timestamped and attributed. Computer vision captures trailer and asset IDs and condition without operator input. History searchable by carrier, driver, asset, or time.
layers.qualifier_criterion_copy: A timestamped, attributable gate record is what a validation asks for.

layers.name: Carrier Risk Assessment
layers.caption: Layer 01 turns every DOT scan into a live, tier-coded risk signal at arrival.
layers.rec_why: Fraud walks in at arrival, not at booking. A live signal at the gate is what catches the double-broker your booking check cannot.

questions.question: You check live carrier authority, insurance, and safety at arrival, not just at booking.
You confirm the arriving carrier is the one that was actually booked.
A risky carrier triggers a decision at the gate (stop, document, clear), not a report afterward.

layers.rec_start: pulling live authority, insurance, and safety at arrival, with a tier-coded decision in the lane
layers.exposure_copy: You are treating every carrier the same because the gate cannot tell them apart. A double-brokered or unauthorized carrier looks identical to a trusted one until the trailer is gone.
layers.standard_copy: Authority, insurance, safety, and OOS history checked live at arrival. Every scan returns a tier-coded decision: stop, document, judge, or clear. The arriving carrier is confirmed against the booking.
layers.qualifier_criterion_copy: Live carrier vetting at arrival is what strengthens this criterion.

layers.name: ID Verification
layers.caption: Layer 02 authenticates the driver and matches them to the load, in seconds.
layers.rec_why: A visual glance cannot catch a convincing fake, and nothing ties the driver to the load they came for.
layers.rec_stop: waving IDs through on a glance

questions.question: Driver IDs are authenticated for fakes, not eyeballed.
The driver is matched to the one expected on this load.
Driver identity is captured and logged on both arrival and departure.

layers.rec_start: authenticating every ID for fakes and matching the driver to the load
layers.exposure_copy: A visual glance cannot catch a convincing fake, and nothing ties the driver to the load they came for. This is the exact gap a fraudulent pickup walks through.
layers.standard_copy: The ID is authenticated for fakes, not glanced at, and the driver is matched to the one expected on the load. Identity captured and logged on arrival and departure.
layers.qualifier_criterion_copy: Authenticated, logged driver identity is a core access-control expectation.

layers.name: Load Verification
layers.caption: Layer 03 ties the seal, load images, and BOL to the shipment, so custody is provable and chargebacks are defensible.
layers.rec_why: It turns an unwinnable chargeback into a defensible one, and closes a CTPAT seal-integrity gap at the same time.

questions.question: Seal numbers are captured and checked against the shipment at the gate.
Load and BOL images are captured and tied to the specific shipment, timestamped.
You could defend a damage or shortage chargeback with a custody record from gate to dock.

layers.rec_start: capturing the seal, load images, and the BOL against the shipment at the gate
layers.exposure_copy: Without a captured seal, load images, and a BOL tied to the shipment, custody is a matter of trust. A damage or shortage chargeback becomes your word against theirs, and you usually lose.
layers.standard_copy: The seal is captured and checked against the shipment. Load and BOL images tied to the shipment and timestamped. The record would defend a damage or shortage chargeback, gate to dock.
layers.qualifier_criterion_copy: Seal capture is a named criterion, and the record has to exist to satisfy it.

layers.name: Perimeter Cameras
layers.caption: Layer 04 closes the fence line with cloud video, LPR, and AI detection in the YOS.
layers.rec_why: Passive footage nobody watches is not security. Integrated detection turns it into a response you can act on.
layers.rec_stop: treating the fence line as out of scope

questions.question: The fence line and yard are covered by cameras integrated with your yard view, not a separate silo.
License plate recognition ties every truck at the gate to its check-in.
AI detection flags intrusion, loitering, or tampering and routes it to the right person in real time.

layers.rec_start: tying cameras and plate recognition into the yard view, with intrusion and tamper alerts routed in real time
layers.exposure_copy: The fence line and after-hours yard are blind. Intrusion, loitering, and tampering happen with no alert and no searchable footage to investigate afterward.
layers.standard_copy: Cameras integrated into the yard view, not a silo. Plate recognition ties every truck to its check-in. AI detection flags intrusion, loitering, and tampering, routed in real time.

verdicts.body: All five layers are working. Every known exposure vector has a control behind it, and each event is one auditable record your team, your claims desk, and an auditor can all pull.
verdicts.headline: Defense in depth at the gate.

verdicts.body: Some layers hold, but the open ones are exactly where strategic theft, a paper-clean double-broker, or an unwinnable chargeback walk in. Partial cover reads as full cover right up until the load is gone.
verdicts.headline: Real gaps a coordinated actor can exploit.

verdicts.body: A single control is not defense in depth. When it misses, nothing behind it catches the miss, and the gate has no second line.
verdicts.headline: One layer is doing all the work.

verdicts.body: Right now the yard runs on trust. Nothing reliably confirms who or what enters or leaves, and no record would hold up in a claim or an audit.
verdicts.headline: The gate is verifying almost nothing.

cta_title: Get your full Yard Security Report
intro_copy: This grader is fifteen quick questions that will assess your operation across five layers of yard security. The result is a single security score and summary action plan, no login to see your result.
cta_disclaimer: We use this to prepare your report and follow up. No spam.
qualifier_note: We will add a readiness read to your result.
cta_description: Your scored result, what good looks like at each layer, and a prioritized plan to close your gaps. Prepared for you as a branded PDF.
report_cta_copy: Bring this report to a 20-minute call and we will map each gap to the layer that closes it, on your yard.
report_cta_title: Close your yard security gaps today.
report_recs_none: Every layer is in place. Maintain the baseline and keep instrumenting the metrics that hold it there.
report_recs_intro: In the order that closes the most exposure for the least effort, based on your grade.
report_recs_title: How to shore up your gaps
qualifier_footnote: Positive driver ID and departure logging (Layer 02), an attributed access record (Layer 00), and seal integrity (Layer 03) are the criteria a validation leans on. Terminal produces the operational record; CBP certifies.
qualifier_question: Do you participate in CTPAT, or do your customers require it?
cta_success_message: Your report is open in a new tab. If it did not open, use the button below.

content.text: Terminal closes all five layers on a single gate vision layer, native to the Yard Operating System you already run. Each layer reinforces the next, so the system interlocks instead of leaking at the seams.

report_closing_title: Five layers, one platform, one record
qualifier_strong_copy: Positive driver ID, access logging, business-partner screening, and seal integrity are largely in place. A validation becomes a query, not a scramble.
report_cover_footnote: Generated from the Terminal Yard Security Grader  ·  © 2026 Terminal Industries
qualifier_exposed_copy: The access-control, driver-ID, and seal evidence CTPAT expects is largely missing today. A validation would surface it quickly.
qualifier_partial_copy: The building blocks exist but have gaps. Positive driver identification and a complete access-control record are where CTPAT validations most often expose weakness.
qualifier_report_intro: The layers you close for security also produce the evidence a CTPAT validation expects. Based on your grade, here is where you stand against the criteria most tied to the gate.
qualifier_report_label: Compliance · included because you flagged CTPAT
report_standards_intro: Your gaps are easier to read against a fixed target. Strong yard security meets these standards, regardless of the technology behind them.
report_standards_title: What good looks like, layer by layer
